stories.title: Winston-Salem Open Final — Fery vs. Buse (4 PM ET)

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Fery vs. Buse. Two breakthrough stars. One first ATP title on the line.

The Winston-Salem final is today at 4 PM ET — the last warm-up before the US Open begins Sunday. 🎾 #TFRtennis #WinstonSalem #Tennis #ATPTour

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Ignacio Buse is the first Peruvian player in an ATP final since 2004.

Arthur Fery is making his first-ever ATP final appearance after his Wimbledon SF run.

History on the line in Winston-Salem. #TFRtennis #Tennis #ATPTour #WinstonSalem

facebook.long_form:
It's a final nobody saw coming — and that's exactly what makes it so good.

Arthur Fery and Ignacio Buse will play for the Winston-Salem Open title today at 4 PM ET, completing a week that featured two of tennis' most exciting young players at their breakout best.

Fery, the 24-year-old from Britain who turned heads worldwide with his Wimbledon semifinal run, advanced to his first-ever ATP Tour final after James Duckworth was forced to retire injured during their semifinal. Buse, representing Peru, earned his spot the hard way — defeating Benjamin Bonzi 6-2, 4-6, 6-1 in a match that showcased his growing comfort on hard courts. Buse's appearance marks the first time a Peruvian player has reached an ATP final in 22 years.

Neither player has won an ATP title. One of them will end today with their name on a trophy, and the other will carry the experience into tomorrow's US Open main draw knowing they belong at tennis' highest level.

The last warm-up before the Grand Slam begins. Don't sleep on this one.

Who are you rooting for today — Fery or Buse? 🎾
facebook.image_caption: The Winston-Salem final is set — and two breakthrough stars are playing for history. Fery vs. Buse, today at 4 PM ET. First ATP title up for grabs. Last match before the US Open begins.

stories.title: US Open Main Draw Starts Tomorrow — Full Preview

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
US Open main draw starts TOMORROW.

No. 1 Zverev. No. 2 Alcaraz returning after 4+ months off. No. 3 Djokovic chasing his 25th Grand Slam.

$108M on the line. Biggest prize money in tennis history. #USOpen2026 #TFRtennis #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Sabalenka is chasing a US Open three-peat — something no woman has done since Serena (2012-14).

But she hasn't reached a final since March, and Rybakina's ankle puts the No. 2 seed in doubt.

Women's draw is wide open. #USOpen2026 #TFRtennis #Tennis #WTA

facebook.long_form:
The wait is almost over. The 2026 US Open main draw begins tomorrow, Sunday Aug 30 — and this year's field might be the most wide-open in a decade.

On the men's side, Alexander Zverev enters as the No. 1 seed after Jannik Sinner's withdrawal. But the story everyone is watching is Carlos Alcaraz, the defending champion who hasn't played a competitive match since April 14. Alcaraz returns as the No. 2 seed, four-plus months removed from a wrist injury that kept him out of Roland Garros, Wimbledon, and the entire North American swing. Can he find his rhythm fast enough? Novak Djokovic, at 39, is here chasing his 25th Grand Slam title and showing no signs of slowing down.

On the women's side, Aryna Sabalenka is bidding for something that hasn't been done since Serena Williams was at her peak — three consecutive US Open titles. She's the No. 1 seed and the heavy favorite, though her recent form has been inconsistent since her Miami title in March. The No. 2 seed, Elena Rybakina, is a question mark — she hasn't practiced since twisting her ankle at Cincinnati.

Total prize money this year: $108 million. Records across the board. Arthur Ashe Stadium holds the biggest crowds in tennis.

Who wins the 2026 US Open? Drop your picks below ⬇️

stories.title: Rybakina Hasn't Practiced — Final Status Update Before US Open

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Elena Rybakina still hasn't been on a practice court since her Cincinnati ankle injury — and the US Open starts Sunday.

The No. 2 seed told reporters: "I want to make sure that everything is okay."

Her status remains unresolved. #USOpen2026 #TFRtennis #WTA #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Elena Rybakina hasn't been on a tennis court since she retired from her Cincinnati quarterfinal eight days ago — and the US Open main draw begins tomorrow.

The world No. 2 and No. 2 seed in Flushing twisted her left ankle while trailing Iga Swiatek 1-4 in what had seemed like a routine quarterfinal. She left the court and hasn't returned since. "I haven't been able to practice yet," Rybakina told reporters this week. "I want to make sure that everything is okay. We will try it in the next few days."

The 2022 Wimbledon champion has been through MRI scans and daily treatment. The prognosis isn't dire — she says recovery is going well — but the timeline is tight. Players need weeks, not days, to prep mentally and physically for a Grand Slam. Rybakina is trying to compress that into hours.

If she withdraws, the draw reshuffles and a qualifier moves into the bottom half of the bracket. But Rybakina hasn't withdrawn. She's being cautious, and that itself is encouraging.

We'll know more by Sunday morning.

What do you think — will Rybakina play? 🤔
facebook.image_caption: Elena Rybakina still hasn't practiced since Cincinnati — and the US Open starts tomorrow. The No. 2 seed's fitness is the biggest question mark heading into Sunday.

stories.title: Roger Federer Inducted into Tennis Hall of Fame Tonight

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Tonight at 6:30 PM ET, Roger Federer is officially inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Class of 2026. Newport, RI. Tennis Channel.

A legend's legacy takes its permanent place in the record books. 🏆 #Federer #TFRtennis #Tennis #ITHF

facebook.long_form:
Tonight, at 6:30 PM ET, Roger Federer takes his place among the legends.

The International Tennis Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony is happening right now in Newport, Rhode Island — and Federer, the 20-time Grand Slam champion who retired in 2022 after one of the most celebrated careers in sport, is being officially enshrined as part of the Class of 2026 alongside legendary broadcaster Mary Carillo.

Tennis Channel is broadcasting it live.

It feels fitting that this ceremony falls the night before the US Open main draw begins. Federer won the US Open five consecutive times (2004-2008). His absence from the game since his retirement has been felt every time a player serves an ace on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Tonight, that legacy gets its permanent home.

The ceremony is hosted by Tom Rinaldi. About 30 Hall of Famers are attending. Yesterday, Federer participated in the Celebrity Pro Classic at the Hall of Fame facility.

Whatever you think about the GOAT debate, tonight is a celebration worth pausing for.

What's your favorite Roger Federer moment? Let us know in the comments 🏆
facebook.image_caption: Roger Federer is being inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame tonight — Class of 2026. Newport, RI. Tennis Channel. 6:30 PM ET. A legend's legacy, officially written in stone.

stories.title: Eala's US Open Debut as No. 17 Seed

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Alex Eala enters the 2026 US Open as the No. 17 seed — the highest Grand Slam seeding in Philippine tennis history.

She opens vs. a qualifier Sunday. A nation is watching. 🇵🇭 #USOpen2026 #TFRtennis #Tennis #Eala

facebook.long_form:
Alex Eala has made history before — and tomorrow, she makes it again.

The 22-year-old from the Philippines enters the 2026 US Open as the No. 17 seed, the highest Grand Slam seeding in Philippine tennis history. When the main draw begins Sunday at Flushing Meadows, Eala will walk onto Arthur Ashe Stadium or one of the show courts not as a qualifier, not as a lucky loser, but as a seeded player with expectations.

She's earned it. Eala has gone 22-9 on hard courts in 2026, reached the DC Open final (a WTA 500 event), and defeated Jelena Svitolina, Naomi Osaka, and other top-20 players during her breakout summer. In Cincinnati, she beat Giulio Zeppieri and Irina-Camelia Begu before a tough loss to Amanda Anisimova.

She opens her US Open campaign against a qualifier in Round 1. On paper, it's a manageable draw. In practice, a Grand Slam debut as a seeded player is its own kind of pressure.

The Philippines has waited a long time for a moment like this. Eala's going to deliver it.

Will you be watching Eala's US Open debut? 🇵🇭
facebook.image_caption: Alex Eala enters the 2026 US Open as the No. 17 seed — the highest Grand Slam seeding in Philippine history. She opens Sunday vs. a qualifier. One year can change everything.
